system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's draft is the other side's advocacy and has been reviewed as such.

## Threshold points before the issue list

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim does not bind us.** The Seller's preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We have no record of that. The playbook says Amelia Frost has given **no** written authority for any fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release). We should not treat any point as agreed unless Amelia Frost confirms it in writing, identifying the draft. If the Seller says she agreed, check directly with her, not through the Seller.
2. **The "market context" is the Seller's advocacy, not a benchmark.** Its claims (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) do not change our positions.
3. **The Disclosure Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. We should require an updated or bring-down disclosure for signing and Completion, especially on Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006.

## Issue-by-issue review

| ID | Seller's position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** General liability cap | Cl 12.1: 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** We have no authority to use the fallback, and the Seller's "settled" claim is unverified. |
| **SPA-N-002** De minimis & basket | Cl 12.2: de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, recovery of the excess only | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded | **Reject; counter at 5k / 50k, first-dollar.** The Seller's figures are 5x our position and the excess-only structure would remove the first AUD 250k of every recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003** General claims time limit | Cl 12.3/13: 18 months | 24 months after Completion. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given. | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** The fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004** Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title subject to the general caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** A defect in title or capacity goes to the whole AUD 24m, so a 20% cap and 18-month window would leave the core asset largely unprotected. |
| **SPA-N-005** Fraud carve-out | Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | **Reject; insert an express carve-out.** This is non-waivable under our playbook, and nobody on our side can concede it. |
| **SPA-N-006** Disclosure scope | DL 1.1–1.2: general disclosure of the whole data room (to 22/9/26), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject DL 1.1–1.2 as disclosures; at most, allow the data room as an index.** Blanket disclosure would neutralise the warranties. Require a fair-disclosure standard (enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter) and an updated letter. |
| **SPA-N-007** Buyer knowledge qualifier | Cl 8.3: no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must use named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete cl 8.3.** It includes constructive and adviser knowledge, so it would bar claims for matters we may actively be pricing or indemnifying, including DD-002 to DD-012. |
| **SPA-N-008** Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL 2 admits no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. Not satisfaction on delivery, and not reasonable endeavours alone. | **Reject; make it a hard CP with an evidence requirement.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and a consent whose conditions are unmet may not be effective. |
| **SPA-N-009** Riverlark facility | Release "following Completion." DL 3: about AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, and no discharge. | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion (including the cl 9.2 discharge and any PPSR/registration releases). A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. | **Reject; require payout and release at Completion through the funds flow.** Otherwise we would pay a debt-free price for a company still subject to about AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-control trigger (cl 8.1). |
| **SPA-N-010** Employee bonuses | Excluded from the funds flow as "a matter for the Seller." DL 5 confirms they are absent and silent on on-costs. | AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, other) either itemised as a specific funds-flow or price-adjustment line or expressly seller-funded, with an indemnity | **Reject the silent exclusion.** If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the cost would fall on us unless it is expressly allocated. On-costs need to be confirmed, not assumed. |
| **SPA-N-011** Ironquay IP indemnity | Cl 11.1 limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | Broaden it to cover any failure of the Company to own or have unencumbered rights to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and costs of a confirmatory assignment. Preserve the SOW3 cure (cleared payment of all SOW3 fees triggers transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3). | **Reject the narrow wording; broaden it and keep the cure route.** Ownership turns on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180k figure (DD-010) is not independently verified either way, so obtain bank evidence or Ironquay confirmation rather than assuming it is paid or unpaid. |
| **SPA-N-012** Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" | Covenants to preserve logs, continue the investigation, and give regular updates (scope, access, notification analysis) before Completion. Warranty and disclosure to be updated. Neutral treatment: no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand is assumed in either direction. | **Do not accept "not material"; add investigation and update covenants.** The facts are unresolved (~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, with access unknown), so the protective position is process and information, not a concession or a fixed number. |
| **SPA-N-013** Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary-course operating costs" (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k) | Assessment first: request the contracts, terms, termination rights, accrual status and timing (DD-008 and DD-011 read together). No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Reserve; request information and reject the Seller's characterisation as unsupported.** DL 8 itself says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014** Category separation | Cl 12.3/13: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims. | Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities each in their own regime, with no default override from the general regime | **Reject; reverse the default.** The general limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. The Seller's wording would quietly import a 20% cap and 18 months into title, indemnities and covenants. |
| **SPA-N-015** Title verification | "Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012" | Independent evidence: ASIC company extract and historical searches, share certificates, constitution, PPSR/encumbrance searches over the shares, Seller's corporate authority (board resolution), and any shareholder or third-party consents | **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** It is an internal, Seller-supplied record, and DL 10 concedes it is only the "source relied on." |
| **SPA-N-016** Tax/IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime above" | Treat as **open**. No resolution has been agreed, and neither unlimited liability nor general-regime treatment should be assumed. | **Reject the "settled" characterisation; keep them as open items for negotiation.** Our playbook records them as unresolved, and folding them into the general regime would also breach category separation (N-014). |

## Other points from the Disclosure Letter

- **DL 1.4 (no admission of breach, liability, consent requirement):** This is acceptable as a general reservation only if it does not undercut specific indemnities or conditions precedent. Specify that it does not.
- **DL 7 (office lease, DD-007) and DL 9 (Mossvale, DD-009):** These are not on the issue list. Confirm in diligence that the lease requires only notification and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Add a covenant to give the lease notification.
- **DL 11:** We agree with the Seller's own reservation that the disclosures contain no agreed conclusions. This undercuts the "FINAL" characterisation in the covering note.

## Recommended next steps

1. Respond that we do not accept the positions as agreed, and confirm the authority position directly with Amelia Frost.
2. Issue a mark-up reflecting the playbook positions above, including the fraud carve-out, the separate title/fundamental regime, and the category-separation clause.
3. Send a diligence request covering: Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 evidence; Riverlark payout letter and draft releases; bonus on-cost analysis; Ironquay payment evidence; DD-006 investigation status; Sandbar contracts; and independent title searches.
4. Request an updated Disclosure Letter dated close to signing, with a bring-down at Completion.
=== END ADVICE ===
